# Check or report a website blocked by Xfinity CyberSecure

Xfinity CyberSecure blocks websites that are determined to be potentially unsafe. These sites may have malware, spyware, ransomware, viruses, or phishing attempts that can harm devices or put personal information at risk.

## Check whether a website is blocked

If you are not sure whether a website is blocked by Xfinity CyberSecure, use the Xfinity CyberSecure Website Checker: [spa.xfinity.com/check-url-status](https://spa.xfinity.com/check-url-status).

## Report a website blocked by Xfinity CyberSecure

If a website seems blocked by mistake, submit a review request at spa.xfinity.com. Xfinity will review the request. Most often, an update will be shared within three business days.

To submit a request to have a blocked website reviewed for possible unblocking:

1. Go to [spa.xfinity.com](https://spa.xfinity.com/).
2. Select **Report an issue** at the bottom of the page.
3. Select **I can't reach a website that I want to go to** from the drop-down menu. Then, click **Continue**.
4. Enter the full URL for the blocked site.
5. Enter your email address to get a confirmation email.
6. Add any other comments you’d like to provide.
7. Click **Review**.
8. Review your answers. Then, click **Submit**.

You'll get a confirmation email once Xfinity gets your report, and one after review is completed.

## Additional information

Visit our [Online Support Center](https://www.xfinity.com/support) to find common solutions.

# Sign in to an account on your Mac with a passkey

A [passkey](https://support.apple.com/guide/passwords/aside/glos0930f77c/3.0/mac/27) is a way to sign in to a website account or an app, without needing to create and remember a password. Instead of a password, a passkey uses Touch ID or Face ID to identify you. You can create and save passkeys for websites and apps that support them.

If your Mac or Magic Keyboard has [Touch ID](https://support.apple.com/guide/passwords/aside/glosc8aef3dc/3.0/mac/27), you can sign in with Touch ID. You can also sign in with an iPhone or iPad by scanning a QR code and using Face ID to verify your identity.

## Create a passkey for a new account

1. When you sign up for a new account, enter an account name, then click to submit.

   To create a passkey, [iCloud Keychain must be set up on your Mac](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mh43699).

2. When you see the option to save a passkey for the account, choose how you want to sign in:

   - *Touch ID on your Mac:* Place your finger on the Touch ID sensor.

   - *Scan a QR code with your iPhone or iPad:* Click Other Options.

   - *External security key:* Click Other Options.

## Replace the password for an existing account with a passkey

Go to the website account or app to replace your password with a passkey. The passkey appears in Passwords.

# Blocking content with your Safari web extension

Build content blocking with declarative net request into your Safari web extension.

## Discussion

Add declarative content blocking that works in Safari, Mac web apps, and other browsers to your Safari web extension. This approach blocks content quickly and ensures privacy for users, because the web extension doesn’t need access to the entire web request to make blocking decisions.

Safari web extensions implement declarative content blocking with the Declarative Net Request API common to web extensions on other browsers.

### Request permission to block content

To use the Declarative Net Request API in your Safari web extension, first request permission. In your Xcode project, add the declarative net request permission to the permissions list in your `manifest.js` file.

```javascript
{
 ...
   "permissions": [
    "declarativeNetRequest",
    "activeTab"
  ],
  ...
}
```

For more information about permissions, see [Managing Safari web extension permissions](/documentation/SafariServices/managing-safari-web-extension-permissions).

### Add rulesets to your extension and manifest

You specify rules for content blocking in rulesets, which are files with `json` describing the content blocking rules. Add references to ruleset files that you create in your `manifest.js` file to tell Safari to use them. For example:

```javascript
{
   ..
